newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK says upset as Malaysia cancels visa waivers.
newsitem.headline: HK says upset as Malaysia cancels visa waivers.

text.p: Hong Kong said it was upset on Friday by a Malaysian decision to cancel visa-free access for Hong Kong holders of limited British passports just days before China takes control.
Three million of Hong Kong's 6.4 million of population are eligible to hold the British National Overseas (BNO) passports, which facilitate travel but provide no British residence rights.
Hong Kong travel agents received a fax from the Malaysian Commission here on Wednesday informing them of the change, the South China Morning Post newspaper said.
A Hong Kong government spokesman said Malaysia had not informed it of the plan but "the government was aware of it".
"The Hong Kong government is disappointed about the intention and would try the best to lobby the Government of Malaysia to reconsider its decision," a spokesman said.
A Malaysian Commission spokesman was unavailable.

"This is totally unjustified and unnecessary," Hong Kong immigration director Regina Ip said. "I do not think it is anything to do with immigration problems caused by our people, but is purely symbolic because of the change of sovereignty," she told the South China Morning Post.
About 80 nations allow visa-free access for BNO passport holders at the moment.
The future Hong Kong government will issue its own Special Administrative Region (SAR) passports from next month, the BNO passports will remain valid after the handover.
Dozens of countries have already recognised the SAR passport and granted either visa-free entry or easy visa access.
Malaysia, a popular destination for Hong Kong people, is also witholding visa-free entry from new SAR passport holders, unlike neighbouring countries Singapore and Thailand.
Travel industry sources say Hong Kong people made more than 120,000 visits to Malaysia last year and the present move would certainly harm the travel business.
